newsitem.title: UK: US stocks in London steady, Dow seen inching up.
newsitem.headline: US stocks in London steady, Dow seen inching up.

text.p: U.S. shares were steady to slightly higher in thin European trade on Thursday following Wednesday's 55-point Dow decline.
Dealers here expect Wall Street to start firmer on follow-through buying, noting that the Dow halved its losses in the final hour of trade on Wednesday.
"We could see a bit of buying at the start. The bonds are fairly strong this morning which should help," one dealer said.
Traders here said Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, which caused a shakeout in both U.S. shares and bonds on Wednesday, may be pushed to the background.
"Greenspan fired another warning shot across the market's bow, but he didn't really saying anything terribly shocking," one market maker said.
"The market knows the interest rate cycle has changed but with inflows still strong, the mutual funds don't yet seem to be too concerned."
The March T-bond was up 15/32 at 111-11/32 while the March S&P 500 futures contract rose 2.25 points to 806.00 by 1120 GMT.
U.S. Robotics was up $9.00 at $70.00 after news late Wednesday of an agreed merger with 3Com Corp. The $6.6 billion stock transaction values U.S. Robotics at $68-1/4 in 3Com stock, traders said.
McDonald's Corp, which dropped $2-3/8 on Wednesday after reports that the company was about to launch its biggest ever discounting programme, was trading at its New York closing level of $44-7/8.
Elsewhere, CPC International was up $1/4 at $85-1/4 in further reaction to news of the company's plans to spin off its corn-refining business.
